facts.fact: Connected TV political advertising typically ranges from $25 to $45 CPM, according to the page.
facts.quote: typically ranging from $25 to $45 CPM for political content.

facts.fact: Spending $100,000 in a small market might deliver the same persuadable voter impressions as spending $500,000 in a major market, per the page's illustrative example.

facts.fact: The page places the post-primary introduction period for general election advertising in June-July.
facts.quote: **Post-primary introduction (June-July).** Many general election voters weren't paying attention during the primary.

facts.fact: The page places the summer consolidation period, tied to party conventions, in July-August.
facts.quote: **Summer consolidation (July-August).** Party conventions, both national and state, create natural messaging opportunities.

facts.fact: The page describes September as the traditional Labor Day launch of the general election campaign.
facts.quote: **Labor Day launch (September).** The traditional "start" of the general election campaign.

facts.fact: The page states that advertising intensity peaks in October and that campaigns typically plan their largest spending for the final four to six weeks.
facts.quote: Advertising intensity peaks in October. Campaigns typically plan their largest spending for the final four to six weeks, when voter decision-making crystallizes.

facts.fact: The page advises adjusting campaign timing if 30% or more of a state's voters will cast ballots before election day.
facts.quote: If 30% or more of your state's voters will cast ballots before election day, adjust timing accordingly.

facts.fact: The page recommends placing weekend-oriented advertising Thursday through Saturday, citing strong political audiences in Friday and Saturday news programming.
facts.quote: Advertising placed Thursday through Saturday reaches voters before weekend conversations with family and friends.

facts.fact: The FCC requires broadcasters to maintain public files documenting political advertising purchases.
facts.quote: The FCC requires broadcasters to maintain public files documenting political advertising purchases.

facts.fact: Competitive general elections in medium-sized states typically involve $10 million to $30 million in combined candidate and outside group advertising, according to the vendor's guidance.
facts.quote: Competitive general elections in medium-sized states typically involve $10 million to $30 million in combined candidate and outside group advertising.

facts.fact: Competitive Senate campaigns in general elections typically spend $5 million to $20 million on advertising, according to the vendor's guidance.
facts.quote: Competitive Senate campaigns in general elections typically spend $5 million to $20 million on advertising, with the highest-profile races exceeding these amounts.

facts.fact: Primary Senate campaigns often spend between $500,000 and several million dollars on advertising, depending on state size and competitiveness.
facts.quote: Primary campaigns often spend less, ranging from $500,000 to several million depending on state size and competitiveness.

facts.fact: Campaigns commonly spend 50-60% of their total advertising budget in October alone, according to the vendor.
facts.quote: Campaigns commonly spend 50-60% of their total advertising budget in October alone.

facts.fact: Many Senate campaigns allocate 20-40% of television budgets to streaming, with the percentage increasing each cycle, according to the vendor.
facts.quote: Many campaigns now allocate 20-40% of television budgets to streaming, with percentages increasing each cycle.

facts.fact: The traditional general election advertising push for Senate campaigns begins after Labor Day.
facts.quote: The traditional general election advertising push begins after Labor Day, but campaigns increasingly start earlier to define narratives before opponents.

facts.fact: Campaigns cannot coordinate with super PACs on advertising content or strategy.
facts.quote: Campaigns cannot coordinate with super PACs on advertising content or strategy.
